title: Blood-Crazed Squirrel
text: “Well then… you’re being annoying with that attitude, just like Smoked Meat, so please die.”
“Huh? Wha—!?”
Thwack! Itsuki loosed an arrow, and it punched clean through the knight’s torso, I say.
“Th-this can’t… impossible— this one’s the bounty—”
“Yes, whoever came up with it, the ‘Blood-Crazed Squirrel, Slayer of Nobles’ — that’s me.”
Itsuki strode down from the carriage and answered the fallen knight with a fearless grin.
“Ah… I probably should’ve taken him alive and tortured him instead of killing him. His face was so irritating that I put too much force into it.”
I’d been beaten to the punch. The moment that should’ve been my chance to shine had been stolen right out from under me by Itsuki.
“Ahh… uugh…”
Fiancée looked back and forth between Father’s and Itsuki’s faces with a dumbstruck expression.
“No, wait… um, hold on.”

“What? It’s not like I did this because I wanted to help anyone, you know. The knight was about to turn his blade on his own kingdom’s princess and even tried to cast magic right there. Leaving him alive wouldn’t have led to anything good.”
Itsuki was saying something eerily similar to what I would’ve said myself.
“M-Melty-sama!”
Éclair called out to Fiancée, whose face had gone pale.
“Kawasumi-dono!”
“Well, that’s one more piece of trash gone from this world. I feel quite refreshed.”
“Ahh… geez.”
Father put a hand to his face at this. Itsuki, isn’t your trigger finger just a little too quick, even by your standards?
“Hi-hiiiiin!?”
Sensing the battle, the horses pulling the carriage bolted off just like that.
“Ahh, wait uup—”
“We’ll go catch them—”
“Leave it to us—”
The Filolial-samas went running off to catch the horses that Fiancée and the knights had ridden in on.
“Are you unharmed!?”
When Éclair called out to Fiancée, Fiancée’s face showed a flicker of fear.
“Mel-chan, you okay?”
When Filo-tan called out worriedly too, Fiancée let out a relieved breath. Then Filo-tan turned to face the dead knights.
“So, how’s it feel to try to attack Mel-chan and get stopped before you could? C’mon, tell me, tell me—”
“Eh…”
Fiancée recoiled in horror. Filo-tan!? Even I have to admit, this side of Filo-tan is a bit much!
“Rafumi!”

“Rafumi-chan! Would you please stop teaching Filo-chan such weird things! Seriously! You’re even kicking someone while they’re already dead! Filo, that’s a no-no, okay? Look, the princess is distressed.”
“Ehh? That’s a no-no? Okaay, got it.”

“Oh, what’s the harm? If souls are a real thing, then kicking them while they’re down would still have an effect. Absolutely pathetic of them. If they come back as vengeful spirits, I’ll make sure to dispose of them properly.”
“Itsuki… you really have changed, you know. I wonder if Rishia-san and Emia-san could somehow heal you back to normal…”
Father let out a truly deep sigh at that.
“Luna, let go—!”
“No. This is too stimulating for Ama.”
Meanwhile, while Ren stood there stunned and horrified, Luna-chan had already grabbed him and buried him in feathers.

In any case, Filo-tan, just like Sakura-chan, was blocking Fiancée’s view so she wouldn’t see the knights’ bodies. Still, Filo-tan continuing to pick up Rafumi’s provocations was a real problem. Even Filo-tan doesn’t usually say things like that!
“Um… first of all, Princess, please listen calmly.”
“Y-yes.”
“It looks like the knights who brought you here were plotting some kind of conspiracy, and intended to kill you along with the rest of us… would that be about right?”
It was the same sort of exchange Father had had when we’d stayed in Melromarc.

“Of course, I’m not saying this without grounds. They were making a huge fuss about how the Shield is supposedly evil, and made a show of taking the princess hostage that was way too obviously staged. I’d be happy to escort you back myself, if you like. We have no intention of kidnapping you, and no intention of throwing your country into chaos either.”
It was a scene I’d seen before. But the defenses this time were far more thorough than before, since Éclair and Crocodile Guy were guarding nearby.
“Scheming up every trick in the book to frame Iwatani-dono… honestly, this is truly deplorable.”
“Even with the kingdom’s military strength so badly depleted, to pull something like this… I have to wonder if they actually want to destroy the country.”
“Perhaps it just goes to show how deep-rooted the problem is… but does that mean my father’s efforts were meaningless?”
“Let’s think of this as the final trial needed to drain the poison, so that both our countries can grow better for it. Surely Lord Seaetto would have wished the same.”
Crocodile Guy gently placed a hand on Éclair’s shoulder as she lamented.
“…You’re right. If I give up here, my father’s soul will never find peace.”
Father gave a small smile at the sight of Crocodile Guy and Éclair together like that. He was probably thinking what a good relationship they had.
“It seems that what was meant to bring reconciliation between you Heroes and my father has instead brought only calamity.”
“Don’t worry about it. You’re a victim in all this too.”
“…Thank you very much.”
“So… you were asked to do this by the Queen, but I wonder what we should actually do about it now…”

Father turned his gaze toward me and Rafumi. Hmm… could we get away with acting the same way we had while staying in Melromarc? This time we hadn’t done any good deeds, so I doubted a revolution would break out within the country. Which meant our domestic reputation was probably at the level of that first world, or worse — meaning the environment was fully set up for Melromarc to move against Father, I say.
“Yes. My mother ordered me to come and mediate between my father and you Heroes. But given how things have turned out, I’m truly sorry.”

Still, well… when we first met her, Fiancée really did have this “borrowed cat” sort of meekness about her. In a sense, the Crimson Swine also puts on a similar façade. In that respect, Fiancée is without doubt the Crimson Swine’s little sister. Or so I think, but every version of Fiancée I’ve ever met so far gets indignant and furious whenever I say that. Well, it’s the truth, I say.

“That’s fine. Though, honestly, I don’t think getting along with your father is possible. We have no intention of getting involved in any war, and all we want is to focus on the Heroes’ real duty: facing the Waves. Not unless he can understand that much, anyway…”
“…Right. I believe this time the fault lies not just with my father and sister, but with the kingdom itself. Once I return safely to the castle, I’ll propose exactly that.”
“But… is it really okay to escort you straight back to the castle like this?”
“Isn’t that impossible? She’d obviously get assassinated. Naofumi-san is despised just for being the Shield Hero, and Motoyasu-san’s hated too, and well, look at me — and even Ren-san…”
At that point, everyone’s eyes turned to Ren, who was being held tight by Luna-chan with just his face poking out from a mound of feathers.
“Wha—!? What were you guys talking about? I couldn’t hear a word because Luna wouldn’t let go of me!?”
Ren clearly hadn’t been in any state to follow the conversation.
“Rafumi-chan, how about you disguise yourself as Ren and escort her back? Your reputation in the country is good, and you’d protect her, right?”

Father and I were out of the question, and Itsuki’s reputation had taken a hit thanks to his companions, so naturally, the one active and famous within the country was Ren… or rather, Rafumi, acting as his body double.
“Hmm… interesting. Sure, I’ll take it on. I’ve thought up all sorts of tricks myself, after all.”
The moment Rafumi grinned, everyone around her furrowed their brows.
“Now I’m even more worried. What is she planning to do?”

Leaving things to you is nothing but a constant source of anxiety, I tell you. What in the world are you planning to pull off!? For whatever reason, it seems Rafumi ended up summoning Ren’s companions. Ah, by the way, the knights’ bodies were disposed of in a flash and all evidence erased. It really is a problem that Itsuki keeps killing people at the worst possible moments — if he’d just taken them alive, we could’ve sent them off to Siltvelt to be silenced properly. I think I hear a voice in my head saying “Like you’re one to talk!” but that’s obviously a mistake. I’ve got perfectly good judgment, I say! Ta-daa!
“Speaking from experience, if we take our sweet time here, Fiancée will end up reported missing with zero evidence, and Father will end up a wanted man.”

“So time’s of the essence, huh… though there’s no telling what would happen if we sent Melty-chan straight back to the castle out of nowhere… She seems to have gotten close with Filo, so maybe it’d be good to have her go along as an escort?”
“That’s the plan, but wouldn’t it be good to also bring along some of Azott’s companions while we’re at it?”
Are they nearby, I wondered, but it seemed Ren’s companions were gathering thanks to Rafumi’s summons. As for Fiancée, we had her resting in the carriage so she wouldn’t be caught in another attack.
